title: The logistic equation and its S-curve

commands.speak: Every forecast that says a population, a virus, or a product will keep doubling is wrong in the same way — and this equation is the fix.
The change per moment is r times P, times one minus P over K.
The first piece is compound interest — a hundred rabbits breed a hundred times faster than one.
The bracket is a brake that closes on its own as P climbs toward K.
K is the carrying capacity — what this habitat can actually feed.
Let those two terms run together, and the population traces this.
Halfway to K the brake is exactly half on, and that is the moment growth is fastest — the peak comes before the crowding is visible.
Verhulst wrote it down in 1838 and called the curve logistique; it was forgotten for eighty years, until biologists fitting real counts found it again.
So the S is not two stories glued together — it is one rule whose own success shuts it down.
